title: City of El Cajon, California confirms network security incident; data reported on Rhysida leak site
date_note: NBC 7's report is dated 23 November and gives no earlier day for the data's appearance; the incident's own start date is not stated clearly enough to use.
geo_basis: victim city named in the reports
summary: NBC 7 San Diego reports that City Manager Graham Mitchell confirmed a network security incident at El Cajon and reports that about eight terabytes of data, including undercover police rosters, reportedly appeared on a ransomware leak site. KPBS says Rhysida claims it stole eight terabytes, including IRS documents for more than 1,000 employees and billing information for 250,000 customers; the city did not comment on the claimed data.
plain: NBC 7 and KPBS report that the city of El Cajon confirmed a network security incident. KPBS says the Rhysida group claims to have stolen eight terabytes of city data, including police records; the city did not comment on the claim.
exec: A city confirmed an incident; KPBS says Rhysida claims eight terabytes of data, including IRS documents for more than 1,000 employees.

evidence.quote: claims it has stolen eight terabytes of sensitive data from the City of El Cajon
IRS documents for more than 1,000 employees
the public works and utility billing information for 250,000 customers

validation.note: NBC 7 San Diego and KPBS are two publishers; KPBS says City Manager Mitchell confirmed a network security incident on Sept. 27. KOGO relays NBC 7. The city's own statement was not read; the claimed data are Rhysida's claims and the city did not comment on them.

review.note: stronger than source: NBC 7 says data reportedly appeared on the leak site; summary now says reportedly; figures match KPBS
